about: The root-cause clusters of the accessibility findings ledger (lib/a11y-issues.mjs; tests/AGENTS.md, A11y: the findings ledger and the cluster catalog). A cluster has id, title, an optional tracker (a task id, or a list of them; code, never printed on the page) and match rules: source, then any of checks, kinds, rules, causes, criteria, pages, themes, where, axeIssues. Values in a field are ORed, fields in a rule ANDed, rules in a cluster ORed. A where pattern reads the finding's masked selector, its step, or both joined as '<masked selector> @ <step>'. A finding no rule matches lands in needs-triage; one that two rules match fails lib/__tests__/a11y-issues.test.mjs. triageLimit is the exact number of sampled finding shapes that need triage: lowered when a shape is sorted into a cluster, raised only visibly, in the change that adds one.

clusters.title: The overlay clones split the accessibility tree: the column headers read after the data, each row is exposed twice, the row headers sit apart from their rows, and a screen reader loses the cell's row index
The grid is built from divs with ARIA roles, and its treegrid root holds children the role does not allow
The focus is not returned to the cell after Escape, Enter or a shortcut closes an editor, a menu or the comment editor, and a screen reader does not re-announce the cell

Controls without an accessible name or role: the editor inputs, the native date and time inputs, the select editor, the comment textarea, the filter listbox, the autocomplete list, and the focus catchers
Menu items have no menu parent, the highlighted item carries aria-selected, separators are exposed as menu items, and a screen reader hears the context menu as a table
The accessible name of the Filters "Filter by value" component does not include its visible text
The Filters "Select all" and "Select none" controls are buttons nested inside buttons
Text, icon, checkbox, grid line and focus indicator contrast under 4.5:1 or 3:1 per theme, and a focus indicator that does not show
Drags without a single-pointer or keyboard alternative that does all the drag does, and controls that act on the press or after the pointer left

Content cut off or needing a sideways scroll at 320 px or 200 %, hover content that does not dismiss, controls drawn over each other, a locked orientation, and motion that runs on or ignores the reduced-motion preference
In forced colors the focus, the selected range, the highlighted menu item, the header icons or the grid lines are not drawn
A range extension, a sort and a nested row's level are not announced: no status message reaches the screen reader
Tab walks out of an open modal dialog to the content behind it, which the dialog hides from assistive technology
Pagination and sheets bar buttons, links and checkboxes are smaller than 24 by 24 px, or sit closer than that to their neighbors
VoiceOver names no row number on a cell move, and no column number in WebKit, on a well-formed grid too: the screen reader's behavior, not the grid's (the scenario notes record it)
With autoWrapRow a Tab walk wraps rows and leaves the grid through Ctrl+End then Tab, as the shortcut guide documents
A page has no tab-order or accessibility-tree golden recorded yet
Column headers with no accessible name: the corner and the empty header cells label their cells with nothing
axe's experimental hidden-content rule lists every hidden element for review: the overlay clones' hidden rows, the closed editors and menus
The scrolling holder is not keyboard focusable, though every cell in it is: axe cannot tell and lists it for review
The docs header's "Ask AI" button has an accessible name that does not contain its visible text
The docs framework switcher's tabs have accessible names that do not contain their visible text
An off-screen copy of the docs navigation is hidden from screen readers but still holds focusable links
Links in the docs prose are told apart from the surrounding text by color alone
Docs code block line numbers in the dark theme, and cell text in some examples, fall below 4.5:1 contrast
Scrollable code blocks and tables in the docs cannot be scrolled from the keyboard
Docs embeds have no frame title, custom renderer images have no text alternative, and some example fields have no label
The closed docs assistant keeps its controls in the Tab order, off screen
A code block's copy button stays invisible when it has the keyboard focus
A link in a hidden copy of the navigation takes the keyboard focus, off screen and hidden from screen readers
An example grid keeps the Tab key, and the documented way out (Ctrl+End, then Tab) does not leave it
A code block that scrolls is a focusable region with no name
The / key opens the docs search with nothing focused, and nothing turns it off
Closing the docs assistant or the search does not give the focus back to the control that opened it
The sticky header hides a focused link when Shift+Tab scrolls it to the top of the window
A focus indicator in the docs stands under 3:1 from the colors next to it
An example's text field has no edge or fill that stands 3:1 from the page
In forced colors, the current breadcrumb and the current table-of-contents entry look like the others
Sidebar and card titles are cut off with an ellipsis at 320 px, at 200% zoom and under text spacing
The phone breadcrumbs are cut off with an ellipsis at 320 px
The phone subheader reaches past the viewport at 320 px, where the page cannot scroll to it
Content that does not wrap (inline code, keys, a link in a callout, the not-found page's game) makes docs pages wider than 320 px
Examples overlap the page's controls, clip their text and cut their labels at 320 px, at 200% zoom and under text spacing
Footer links overlap each other at 200% zoom
Each callout is a complementary landmark named by its type, and the two pagination navigations share a name, so the landmark list repeats names
Docs pages skip heading levels inside the main content
The framework variants of a docs page share one title
Some docs links are named "here", "read more" or "learn more", which says nothing out of context
The not-found page's title does not hold its heading
